document_type: cross-spec orchestration and deployment specification bundle

findings.title: Recovery event append target is undefined after session-closing reconciliation
findings.location: SPEC-00 §2 Seam C, paragraph beginning "**Incomplete turns (crash, disconnect, kill mid-turn):**"
findings.evidence: "On the next session start, SPEC-03 must perform state reconciliation ... If the reconciliation detects model state that diverges from the DHF record, SPEC-03 records a reconciliation event via `DhfLedger.AppendRecoveryEventAsync`."
findings.problem: The contract does not specify which `session_id` receives that recovery event when the prior session has already been closed due to `heartbeat_timeout` or `superseded_session`.
findings.why_it_matters: `AppendRecoveryEventAsync` cannot be implemented consistently: appending to the closed session conflicts with the closure invariant, while appending to the new session breaks causal traceability unless a cross-session link is defined.
findings.proposed_fix: Define, per trigger, whether the recovery event is appended to the existing session, the newly opened session, or a separate recovery container; if it can land in a new session, add explicit linkage fields such as `source_session_id` and `source_entry_id`.

findings.title: Decoration persistence seam uses raw `JsonElement` instead of a canonical cross-module contract
findings.evidence: SPEC-00 says the pipeline assembles a "`VocabularyResolutionDecoration` payload"; SPEC-07 defines `public JsonElement? DecorationPayload { get; init; }`; SPEC-04 defines `public required JsonElement Payload { get; init; }`.
findings.problem: The prose names a specific decoration type, but the actual seam contract is untyped JSON with no shared schema, required fields list, or validation owner defined at the boundary.
findings.why_it_matters: SPEC-07, SPEC-05, SPEC-04, and SPEC-06 can drift independently; malformed or version-skewed decorations can be persisted without deterministic rejection, creating integration churn and weak test coverage.
findings.proposed_fix: Define a shared DTO or formal JSON schema for `VocabularyResolutionDecoration` (including `schemaVersion` and required fields) and specify which module validates it before `AppendTurnAsync` persists it.

findings.title: Auth-mode detection relies on an unspecified `/health` negotiation contract
findings.evidence: "Add-in detects which mode the orchestrator is running by inspecting the WWW-Authenticate header on the initial HTTPS probe to `/health`"
findings.problem: No response contract is defined for `/health`: method, status codes, header values, auth requirements, and proxy/header-stripping behavior are all unspecified.
findings.why_it_matters: The add-in cannot implement or test v1/v2 auth-mode negotiation deterministically, so deployment-mode switching will depend on out-of-band assumptions.
findings.proposed_fix: Define the exact unauthenticated discovery endpoint contract with example responses and fallback behavior, or replace probing with an explicit configured auth mode.

findings.title: Permanent add-in failure is misreported as `MalformedEnvelope`
findings.evidence: "The `MessageDispatcher` rejects all incoming messages with `AddinProtocolErrorMessage(ErrorCode = MalformedEnvelope, ErrorText = \"Add-in permanently failed; restart SolidWorks.\")`."
findings.problem: `MalformedEnvelope` describes bad wire framing, not an internal terminal host failure.
findings.why_it_matters: The orchestrator cannot distinguish protocol corruption from a permanently failed add-in, so retry, quarantine, telemetry, and user-remediation behavior will be wrong.
findings.proposed_fix: Introduce a dedicated error code/message for terminal add-in failure and define orchestrator handling for that condition.

findings.title: Session closure reasons expire after 7 days because they are only logged, not durably stored
findings.location: SPEC-00 §6 "DHF Session"; DEPLOYMENT v1→v2 §7 v1 Contract
findings.evidence: SPEC-00: "Closure reasons ... are recorded in the orchestrator's structured logs ... NOT in the DHF schema." DEPLOYMENT §7: "Retention: Railway default (7 days)"
findings.problem: The only authoritative source for closure attribution is an ephemeral log sink with short retention.
findings.why_it_matters: Operators will be unable to investigate older sessions or explain why a session ended once the Railway log window expires.
findings.proposed_fix: Require durable export/retention for session-closure events or persist a clearly non-audit-chain closure-reason record outside the DHF hash chain.

findings.title: `sequence_number` was removed from hash inputs without a replacement integrity rule
findings.evidence: The change removes `"sequence_number"` from `HashedColumns` with the rationale that "sequence_number ordering is enforced by previous_hash which IS hashed."
findings.problem: The spec no longer integrity-protects the persisted order field, and it does not define a validator contract that derives authoritative order solely from `previous_hash`.
findings.why_it_matters: Sequence/order metadata can be altered without changing `record_hash`, which can produce inconsistent replay, viewer ordering, and audit interpretation.
findings.proposed_fix: Either restore `sequence_number` to the hashed material or explicitly redefine validation and query ordering to use a chain walk from `previous_hash` plus supporting DB constraints.
